items.title: AI-designed proteins enable a new generation of RNA transporters
items.excerpt: A team combined functional protein building blocks with a generative-AI-designed structural scaffold to build STV-C8, an RNA delivery vehicle. In cell culture STV-C8 delivered RNA cargo more efficiently than the virus-like particles and lipid nanoparticles tested, and in pigs it carried CRISPR/Cas9 into muscle tissue without observable toxicity.

items.title: Agentic AI accelerates search for crops that can harvest critical minerals
items.excerpt: Oak Ridge National Laboratory built an agentic AI system that cut plant-trait analysis from hundreds of hours of manual work to a few minutes. It screened 360 pennycress plants to find nickel-tolerant lines usable for phytomining.

items.title: War drama Pressure depicts D-day's weather forecast—what we found when we recreated the challenge using modern systems
items.excerpt: Andrew Charlton-Perez and Ed Hawkins re-ran the D-Day forecast with ECMWF's AIFS machine-learning forecasting system using newly digitised 1944 observations. The AI captured the North Sea storm and would have supported delaying the invasion from June 5 to June 6, but it underestimated the wind and cloud on June 6 — expert interpretation still mattered.

items.title: Why scientists are looking to provoke disagreement among AI brain models
items.excerpt: Columbia University researchers synthesise 'controversial stimuli' — images engineered to make competing computational brain models disagree — then show them to people to see which model matches human perception. The method indicated the visual system blends fast discriminative computation with generative modelling rather than relying on one mechanism.

items.title: In a third of cases, AI chatbots wrongly reassure sleep apnea patients that their symptoms aren't serious
items.excerpt: Researchers ran 700 simulated consultations across ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, DeepSeek and Grok with fictional obstructive sleep apnea patients. Correct specialist referral advice fell to 64% when the patient downplayed symptoms, and to 22-32% in the most severe cases, with chatbots offering lifestyle tips instead. Presented at the European Respiratory Society Congress.

items.title: How introverted or extroverted you are may influence how you use AI
items.excerpt: New personality research suggests how people relate to their inner and outer worlds shapes how they approach generative AI, with extraverted participants reporting greater affiliation with an AI that used extraverted language.

items.title: When Thought Loses Its Address
items.excerpt: A study of freely interacting communities of LLM agents found collective states that fed back into each agent's decisions. On mathematical problems, correct agents exerted more influence than incorrect ones, producing an emergent truth-seeking tendency with no central coordinator.

items.title: AI dominates the 4th International Congress of Basic Science in Beijing
items.excerpt: More than 800 delegates from over 30 countries met in Beijing in August 2026, where AI dominated the programme. Fields medallist Martin Hairer said AI won't end mathematics but will transform how it is carried out, while speakers insisted human creativity and independent thinking remain essential.

items.title: Planetary prediction engine: Automating global models via Earth AI
items.excerpt: Google Research released the Planetary Prediction Engine, an autonomous system that runs the whole geospatial modelling workflow from data discovery to model training. It reached 76.8% mean R2 on CDC health indicators versus 60% for manual pipelines, doubled food-security mapping accuracy in Nigeria and hit 83.3% recall on Ebola outbreak hotspots in the DRC.

items.title: GlucoFM: Foundation model for continuous glucose monitoring
items.excerpt: GlucoFM is a self-supervised foundation model for continuous glucose monitoring with a dual-stream architecture that separates slow glycemic trends from short-term deviations. Across four clinical cohorts and seven metabolic prediction tasks it averaged 5.8 percentage points higher PR-AUC than baselines, with strong cross-dataset and few-shot transfer.

items.title: BenchMIRT: What are LLM benchmarks actually measuring?
items.excerpt: Ai2 applied multidimensional item response theory across 100 LLMs and more than 34,000 benchmark questions to audit what evaluations actually measure. Safety and general reasoning emerged as the two dominant latent dimensions, and the method can cut evaluation sets by 90% while preserving predictive accuracy.

items.title: Why organic chemistry may help build AI that can explain its answers
items.excerpt: A Chemical Reviews paper from the University of Notre Dame argues that organic chemistry's messy, data-poor problems are forcing AI toward interpretability, uncertainty quantification and built-in physical law. The authors tie those constraints to self-driving laboratories and more reliable scientific AI.
